But the worked example a(b+c)* applies union, then star, then concatenation. A student following the figure order will not get the same step sequence.

problem: The answer says merging the first machine's final with the second machine's start 'can add or remove paths through other ε-links'. In Thompson's construction both states are freshly created: f₁ has no outgoing edge other than the ε we add, and s₂ has no incoming edge, so for this construction the merge preserves the language. The stated reason is not the real reason.
fix: Answer: Thompson's construction never merges, because merging is only safe when the first final has no other outgoing ε-links and the second start has no other incoming links. Keeping the two states and joining them with one ε-transition keeps the induction modular and stays correct even when a sub-machine is reused or its final already carries ε-links (as in R*).
